newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FOCUS-Dutch Rabobank 96 profits jump, sees growth.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Dutch Rabobank 96 profits jump, sees growth.

text.p: Dutch cooperative bank Rabobank Nederland BA announced a 14 percent rise in 1996 net profits on Wednesday and forecast a considerable leap in earnings in the current year.

The unlisted bank also unveiled hidden reserves of 3.5 billion guilders ($1.86 billion) and indicated provisions for loan losses in 1997 would be lower than 1996 as a result of previous over-provisions.
Rabobank, the third largest bank in the Netherlands after ABN AMRO and ING Groep, also vowed to retain its mutual structure into the next century.
Unveiling the outcome of what it called another successful year, it said 1996 profit was 1.63 billion guilders, another annual record, compared with 1.43 billion in 1995.
"Strong increases in both domestic and international customer demand for the Rabobank Group's products and services generated double-digit growth in most business areas," the bank said.

Executive board chairman Herman Wijffels said profit growth would have exceeded 20 percent, if not for more than 300 million guilders of provisions related mainly to the planned single European currency and the millennium.
The result was powered by vigorous growth in all activities, which increased income by 12.1 percent to 9.65 billion guilders.
The bank said the growth was expected, partly because of some new activities in the Netherlands and abroad, including South Africa, New Zealand, Vietnam, Russia and Poland.
At a news conference, Wijffels said Rabobank's profit growth in 1997 should be in line with the increase in business volumes.
He said business volumes had increased at an average of about eight percent in recent years, adding that major growth in volume terms was expected in 1997.
"It is too early to give a proper forecast ... but we expect a considerable profit increase should be possible (in 1997)," Wijffels said.
Rabobank said operating profit before tax climbed 13.9 percent to 2.37 billion guilders in 1996 from 1995.
The bank said demand for banking services grew strongly and lending and provision income had seen a double digit rise.
More than half the growth in the credit portfolio was due to increased demand from personal consumer clients, especially for home loans, as a result of low interest rates.
Interest rate profits, the difference between interest income and interest expense, increased 10.8 percent to 7.08 billion guilders, despite stable interest margins.

Commission income rose 16.9 percent to 1.25 billion guilders, helped by a favourable share market, while sales and profit taking contributed to a 23.8 percent hike in income from securities and participating interests to 203 million guilders.
But results from financial transactions fell five percent to 258 million guilders, against the expected trend for the other major Dutch banks, which are more exposed to financial markets
